[Zhang and Nanda](https://arxiv.org/html/2309.16042v2) establish that corruption choice, evaluation metric and patching window can materially change localization results; they favor realistic counterfactual replacements and logit differences over probability alone. Makelov’s verified ICLR 2024 paper is *Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching*, by Aleksandar Makelov, Georg Lange, Atticus Geiger and Neel Nanda. It shows that successful subspace interventions can activate dormant pathways rather than identify naturally used features. This does not establish that full-vector residual-state replacement suffers the same projection-induced illusion—or certify it as faithful. A full-vector patch establishes an intervention effect under specified conditions, not unique feature localization. [Conference record](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/70b8505ac79e3e131756f793cd80eb8d-Abstract-Conference.html).

Practical controls for frozen NextItNet, inferred from these methodological concerns: specify the exact residual boundary, tensor layout and patched positions; verify hook execution counts, cached tensors and replacement values. Require self-patching to reproduce baseline scores, a deliberately changed patch to affect the intended tensor, and hook removal in `finally`. Use realistic donor histories, bidirectional donor/recipient swaps, unrelated-donor controls and held-out pairs. Full-vector replacement still creates hybrid states when other positions retain recipient activations; causal convolutions subsequently mix them. Compare position-local patches with coherent receptive-field/window replacements, and report raw score-margin changes alongside ranking changes rather than treating recovery as semantic proof.

Verify diagnostic/deployed scoring parity using identical checkpoints, routing, padding, truncation, final nonpadding readout, candidate IDs, masking and score transformations; compare actual scores numerically. Bound runtime through explicit limits on users, donors, layers and passes, batched patches, chunked catalog scoring, bounded caches and measured synchronized GPU latency. Use both `eval()` and `inference_mode()`; the latter does not enable evaluation mode. [PyTorch documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.grad_mode.inference_mode.html).
